title: Rowdy Hecklers in Greek Theatres
hook: If an actor fumbled a single line in Athens, 14,000 spectators threw rotten figs, olives, and stones.

scenes.text: Attending the Theatre of Dionysus in Athens wasn't a quiet cultural night out—it was an all-day, wine-soaked civic spectacle with 14,000 rowdy spectators.

scenes.text: Performances of tragedies and comedies were high-stakes competitions where playwrights like Sophocles and Aristophanes competed for the golden ivy wreath.

scenes.text: Audiences brought baskets stuffed with snacks: garlic, barley cakes, dried figs, and heavy terracotta flagons of unmixed wine.

scenes.text: If an actor mispronounced a syllable or delivered a flat punchline, thousands of spectators drummed their heels against stone benches, hissing and booing.

scenes.text: They hurled rotten fruit, olive pits, and even cobblestones onto the stage, forcing terrified actors to flee mid-monologue.
